name: Micro Texture Analysis
description: Analyzes micro-level texture patterns invisible to human eye
algorithm: Micro Texture Analysis — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes micro-level texture patterns for image forensic analysis following Haralick et al. (1973):

1. **Micro-Texture Extraction**: Fine-grained texture features are extracted at the pixel level using high-pass filtering and texture energy measurements. Micro-textures (texture details at the 1-5 pixel scale) capture the finest observable detail in the image.

2. **Texture Co-occurrence Analysis**: Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrices (GLCM) are computed at small displacements (1-3 pixels) in multiple directions. GLCM-derived features (contrast, correlation, energy, homogeneity, per Haralick et al.) characterize the micro-texture properties.

3. **Natural vs. Synthetic Texture Discrimination**: Natural micro-textures arise from physical surface properties (material roughness, surface structure) filtered through the camera's imaging pipeline (lens MTF, sensor integration). AI-generated micro-textures arise from the generator's learned distribution. These differ in: (a) statistical higher-order moments, (b) directional properties, (c) scale-dependent behavior.

4. **Micro-Texture Spatial Consistency**: The consistency of micro-texture statistics across the image is checked. All regions captured through the same camera show consistent micro-texture properties. Regions with different micro-texture statistics (e.g., a face with different micro-texture than the background) indicate potential manipulation or AI generation.

5. **Texture Authenticity Scoring**: Micro-texture features are combined into a forensic score. The score measures how well the observed micro-textures match expectations for natural imaging vs. AI generation, with region-specific scoring to highlight inconsistent areas.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through micro texture analysis analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used

references.title: Haralick, R.M. et al. (1973). Textural Features for Image Classification. IEEE TSMC.
Corvi et al. (2023). On the Detection of Synthetic Images Generated by Diffusion Models. ICASSP.
